In the afternoon, you will visit El Ocaso Farm at an altitude of approximately 1,500 metres in the Central Andes. The road winds through coffee bushes, green hillsides and humid mountain forest.

A local expert will explain how coffee is grown in the region's volcanic soils, how the cherries are picked by hand and why selective processing is used for the finest varieties. You will then visit a typical country house, where the beans are roasted over a wood fire right in the kitchen.

The route includes several viewpoints. You will watch the beans being dried and see the processing plant at work before sampling freshly brewed coffee. At the end of the excursion, coffee lemonade is served in the farm's main house.

## Tayrona: Immerse Yourself in a Caribbean Paradise

Immerse yourself in unspoilt nature. An underwater world teeming with life. One hundred species of animals and birds.

Just 25 kilometres east of Santa Marta, Tayrona National Park is a paradise of wild Colombian landscapes and the mysteries of ancient civilisations. Its 12,000 hectares of pristine jungle invite you into the tropical forest at the foot of the Sierra Nevada mountain range. Azure lagoons and white-sand beaches offer a place to relax beside the turquoise waters of the Caribbean Sea. Explore a rich underwater world and its remarkable variety of marine life. Look out for exotic birds, playful monkeys and other mammals that inhabit the park.

## Experience the Spirit of Adventure

Uncover the secrets of the past through Tayrona archaeological sites. Discover the heritage of the ancient Tayrona civilisation as you visit the ruins of settlements, temples and other archaeological remains. Follow scenic tropical trails leading to waterfalls, hidden lagoons and secluded beaches. Discover local traditions and enjoy dishes from traditional Colombian cuisine. Feel close to nature amid the beauty of the rainforest and the tranquillity of the coast. Tayrona brings together history and nature, adventure and peaceful seclusion.

One of the principal monuments is the Hieroglyphic Stairway from the Classic period. Its 63 steps are covered in inscriptions, while balustrades decorated with images of snakes and birds line either side. Exploring these monuments reveals why Copán is called the "Athens of Mesoamerica".

After breakfast, accompanied by your guide, you will head to one of Rio de Janeiro's leading attractions: the world-famous Christ the Redeemer statue rising above the summit of Mount Corcovado.

A special tourist train takes you from the foot of the mountain along a winding track through the beautiful Tijuca rainforest. With luck, you may spot some of the local wildlife along the way: toucans, monkeys and armadillos.

At the summit of Corcovado, approximately 700 metres above sea level, stands the famous 38-metre Christ the Redeemer statue, one of Brazil's most recognisable symbols.

Yet the statue itself is only part of the experience. Standing beside it, you will be amazed by the spectacular panorama of Rio de Janeiro. From this height, it almost feels as though you are soaring over the city with the birds. Before you stretch Guanabara Bay, Maracanã Stadium, Sugarloaf Mountain, Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, and Gávea Mountain.

The whole of Rio de Janeiro lies before you in all its splendour.
